summary: Frontend-only testing of AUTO-FIT thermal label rendering across 3 sizes x 2 products (6 combos), plus VALIDADE/ALÉRGICOS styling and print/batch flows. 4/6 auto-fit combos pass; 2 combos CLIP the content (auto-fit iteration oscillates and does not converge). VALIDADE, ALÉRGICOS, print-current, and print-batch (2+3=5 pages) all pass.

ui_bugs.issue: 80x50 with 'Molho de Tomate Artesanal' clips: content rendered height 208.6px > outer 189.0px (over by ~19.6px, fill_h=1.104). Applied transform scale=1.033 (>1) despite content already overflowing.
80x60 with 'Pão de Hambúrguer Brioche' clips: content rendered height 246.8px > outer 226.8px (over by ~20px, fill_h=1.088). Applied transform scale=1.066 (>1).

action_items: Fix the auto-fit iteration in /app/frontend/src/components/ThermalLabel.jsx so it converges when width↔wrapping↔height coupling oscillates. Suggested fixes: (a) After the iteration loop, do a final downscale check: measure scrollHeight AT the width `OW/s` actually applied, then only ACCEPT that s if `s * natH_final <= OH`; if not, keep reducing s in a small loop until the constraint holds. (b) Or clamp s to `min(s, OH/scrollHeight_at_current_width)` in a final settle pass. (c) Alternatively, treat s as monotonically non-increasing during iteration (never grow s once it has been reduced) — this guarantees no-clip. Currently the last iteration recomputes s from scrollHeight of the previous width, so the applied width and applied scale may be inconsistent, yielding scale > 1 even when content exceeds outer.
Re-test 80x50 Molho and 80x60 Brioche after fix; the other 4 combos are fine.
critical_code_review_comments: ThermalLabel.jsx: iterative fixed-point does not guarantee `s * natH <= OH`. The final scale can be >1 while content still overflows because scrollHeight is remeasured under a different width than the one that will be applied post-scale. Add a monotonic-decrease invariant on s, or a final safety clamp.
The loop terminates after 6 iterations regardless of convergence; consider convergence check `|s_i - s_{i-1}| < eps` with a hard upper bound and a final downscale safety pass.

rca of the issue: The auto-fit in ThermalLabel.jsx uses a 6-iteration fixed-point that couples content width (`OW/s`) to natural height (scrollHeight) to scale (`s = OH/natH`). Because line-wrapping is discontinuous, when the width crosses a wrap threshold between iterations, scrollHeight jumps and s oscillates between values that don't correspond. The final block recomputes s from `scrollHeight` measured at the last-set width, then updates the width to `OW/s` and sets `transform: scale(s)` — but does NOT remeasure scrollHeight after the width change. If the new width triggers a re-wrap that increases the natural height, the applied scale (>1 in these cases) actually multiplies content that was already taller than outer, producing overflow. Reproduction: 80x50 Molho and 80x60 Brioche — the natural (unscaled) content height at width `OW/s` exceeds OH, yet scale s>1 is applied. Mitigation: add a final downscale safety pass — after applying width `OW/s`, measure scrollHeight again and set `s = min(s, OH/scrollHeight)`; iterate at most 2-3 more times until `s * scrollHeight <= OH + epsilon`. Alternatively, make s monotonically non-increasing across iterations.
